correctness.rationale: All three nonzero vectors of a binary rank-two code are permuted by GL2(F2), reducing linear isomorphism minimization exactly to six matchings. Each crossed pair is improved or maintained by uncrossing, proving optimal sorted ratios. Pairwise ratio comparison yields D≤n, and equality requires a weight-one and weight-n word in one code and equal nonzero weights in the other. Binary column-count algebra gives exactly (1,n-1,n) and (2t,2t,2t), 1≤t≤floor(n/3), and these constructions attain n. The sorted triple uniquely determines a binary rank-two code modulo coordinate permutation; n=2 is exceptional. The actual embedded verify.py separately checks 21,096 generators and 19,902 profile pairs with exact fractions; those tests corroborate rather than substitute the all-length argument.

value.rationale: This is a natural global extremal invariant for the newly introduced code-distortion framework. It replaces a general n² upper bound with a sharp n law in the first nontrivial binary dimension, explicitly identifies the distortion geometry with a projective metric on weight profiles, and classifies every maximizing pair for all lengths. The statement is not an arbitrary finite parameter calculation or a mere numerical refinement: it gives a universal structural extremal theorem and equality rigidity, useful as an exact benchmark for higher-dimensional distortion and algorithms.
